summary:
## Phoenix Drawing: Key Concepts & Techniques

This document outlines the key artistic choices and techniques used to create a vibrant phoenix illustration.

### Outline Strategy
- **Initial Linework**: A fine **0.05mm wine-colored Copic Multiliner** was used for the initial outlines, providing a warm alternative to black ink.
- **Selective Outlining**: Outlines were concentrated on the phoenix's head, body, and foreground wing.
- **Fading Effect**: The outlines were intentionally faded out towards the tail. This area was left to be defined later with colored pencils, creating a softer, more integrated look.
- **Composition**: A **black comic panel** was drawn in the background, with the phoenix overlapping it. This helps the main subject pop from the page.

### Coloring with Copic Markers
A key decision was to use a **warm color palette** and avoid cool grays on the phoenix itself to maintain its fiery essence.

#### Color Palette & Application:
- **Head**: **Buttercup Yellow** and **Cadmium Yellow** applied in streaks to simulate a feathered texture.
- **Beak**: **Egg Shell** with **Cool Gray 3 & 5** for subtle shading.
- **Eye & Mouth**: **Rose Red** (mouth) and a mix of **Honey**, **Apricot**, & **Crimson** (eye).
- **Body**: A base of **Honey**, shaded with **Apricot** and the bolder **Rose Red**.
- **Wings (Foreground)**: A complex blend to create a focal point, using **Cardinal**, **Amethyst**, **Crimson**, **Rose Red**, and **Pure Pink** markers.
- **Wings (Background)**: Colored with the same palette but in a simplified, "blurred" style to create depth.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> To preserve the phoenix's warmth, **cool gray markers were avoided** for shading on the bird itself. Instead, a warm **Rose Red** was used, which blended surprisingly well with the oranges and yellows.

### Detailing with Pencils & Paint
- **Tail Feathers**: After a base coloring with Copic markers (**Pure Pink**, **Rose Red**, **Lavender**), **Prismacolor pencils** were used to add outlines and shading.
  - **Violet** for dark underside shading.
  - **Mulberry** to define the feather midpoints.
- **Highlights**: A **Uni-ball Signo Broad white ink pen** was used throughout to add sharp highlights, especially on the feathers and around the phoenix's silhouette.
- **Final Effects**: **Acrylic paint** was flicked onto the page to create glowing sparks and particle effects, adding a magical final touch.

### Background
- **Contrast**: The background was filled with clouds using **Cool Gray markers (3, 5, & 7)**. This cool, muted background provides strong contrast, making the warm colors of the phoenix appear more vibrant.
transcription:
## Introduction & Outline Tools

Hi everyone and welcome to this fantasy art Friday video. In this video, I'm going to be working on a drawing of a phoenix. Ever since I started working on these fantasy art videos, lots of you have asked me to work on a drawing of a phoenix, and I feel like it's a great way to start the new year as my first drawing of 2017, with it symbolizing renewal and time.

Also, before working on the drawing, as some of you might have noticed, I've recently upgraded my microphone so it should sound a lot better in this video. For those of you who are interested, I got the Blue Yeti, and it's been amazing so far. So to start off for the outlines of this drawing, I decided to use something a little bit different than some of my recent drawings, and I decided to use a wine colored Copic multiliner, which is 0.05 mm. It's extremely fine, so it gave me that extra control over the line work, and I just love the color of the outlines.

## Outline Strategy & Composition

I should also mention I decided to try something a little bit different with the outlines for this drawing. I didn't want to add outlines all over the Phoenix. I wanted to focus all the outlines to the Phoenix, his head, body, and wings, and then I wanted to fade the outlines outwards towards the tail. And my idea was to leave those until later on when I added the coloring with the Copic markers. And then I wanted to add some bright colored outlines with Prismacolor pencils.

So I basically wanted to fade the outlines towards the tail and then carry them on with pencils later on. I also decided to add the outlines of a black comic panel, having it in the background with the Phoenix overlapping with the wings and its tail, just to make the Phoenix stand out from the page.

## Coloring the Phoenix's Head

After the outlines, it was time to work on the coloring. And for the coloring of this drawing, I used Copic markers. I used Buttercup yellow and Cadmium yellow to add the coloring around the Phoenix's head, using streaks of coloring to try and create that feathered effect. And then to add the coloring to the Phoenix's beak, I used an egg shell marker, adding some extra shading around the area with a cool gray three and five.

For the coloring inside the Phoenix's mouth, I used a rose red marker, and to add the coloring to its eye, I used a mixture of Honey, apricot and crimson. To add any highlights around these areas, I used a uni-ball signo broad white ink pen.

## Coloring the Body & Preserving Warm Tones

For the coloring of the fethers on the back of the Phoenix's head, for the curved ones, I used a mixture of rose red and lavender. And then for the extended feathers that reach up towards the top of the drawing, I used a mixture of honey and apricot. Moving on from that, for the coloring of the feathers on the Phoenix's body, I added a base layer of coloring with a honey marker and then added some shading around each feather with the apricot marker.

Once those base layers had been added, it was time to add some extra shading around the lower part of the Phoenix and to add some extra shading around the outer edges. For this, I used the rose red marker which, at first I wasn't sure about using. I didn't know if it was going to blend well, but after testing on some paper to the side of me, they seem to blend really well and it continued to add a really nice warm tone to the coloring of this drawing.

There's a reason why I didn't use the cool gray markers for the coloring of the Phoenix that much. I felt like they would take away from the warm tone that the Phoenix really should give off. I felt like if I added the cool tones over the top of that it would really take away from the effect of the Phoenix, and I intended to use the cool gray markers later on for the background to add that contrast. For the coloring of its feet, I decided to use the same colors that I used for the feathers on the top of its head, that being rose red and lavender.

## Coloring the Wings for Depth

Once I finished working on the coloring of the body, I then wanted to work on the wing in the foreground. I wanted to focus most of the detail of the drawing to this area, really make it stand out and show up, especially overlapping the comic panel, just really making this area stand out. So for the top of the wing, I blended upwards from the body, adding the same coloring with the honey and the apricot markers.

And then I really wanted to change up the coloring of the wing and make it very different. So I brought out a cardinal marker, which is a very dark deep red, and I used it to add a thick outline going around the outer edges of each of the inner feathers on the inner part of the wing. And once I'd added those outlines, I then used an amethyst marker over the top of this to add the rest of the coloring to those inner feathers. I also used a crimson marker to add lots of coloring to this area. Crimson is probably one of my most used pens. I've had to buy refills because I use this pen so much, and I love the color.

I used it to add lots of coloring over the top of this area, blending some of the shading downwards. And then I also used it to add some outlines going around each of the main feathers around the outer edge of this Wing, really making them stand out with a thick border. And then for the rest of the color of those main feathers, I used rose red and pure pink. I used the same colors for the other wing but in a much more simplified way, keeping this area much more blurred and less detailed to keep it in the background and focusing most of the detail to this wing in the foreground and making that area really stand out.

## Defining the Tail with Prismacolor Pencils

And after working on the wings, it was then time to work on the tail and all of the long tail feathers. For this, I used a mixture of pure pink and rose red for the first layers, adding lots of coloring going all the way to the tip of each feather. And then after that, I used a lavender marker to add some shading to the underside of each long feather, really trying to define the shape of each individual feather and making sure they stand out as much as possible.

This is why I left the outlines before and I decided not to use the pen for the outlines of these areas, and I wanted to leave it to prismacolor pencils. This is something that I haven't tried before, but I really wanted to see the effect it would give. So I opted to use a violet prismacolor pencil to add some dark shading around the undersides of each feather and blending it upwards by adding some lighter shading. After that, to define the midpoint of each feather, I used a mulbury prismacolor pencil and blended it upwards towards the Phoenix's back.

## Adding Final Details & Background

Once the tail feathers have been colored, I then tried to use the prismacolor pencils to add some extra details around the Phoenix, adding some extra feathers around the Phoenix's head, adding some white lines to some of the edges of the feathers of the wing, and using the darker Violet pencil to show up and define the outlines of each feather inside the wing.

Afterwards, for the background of this drawing, I decided to use a mixture of cool gray 3, five and seven to add some layers of cloud, starting with cool gray 3 at the top and adding some darker layers of clouds with the cool gray 5 and seven towards the bottom of the drawing, and just kind of blending it upwards and keeping it as smooth as possible. To make sure that the Phoenix would stand out from this, I made sure to use my uni ball highlighter pen to add some highlighting going all the way around the Phoenix and to really sharp the highlights on the feathers.

And after that it was time for the final stages of adding some detailing, in which I decided to try something completely different, and I opted to use some acrylic paint, adding some particle effects and some sparks going around the Phoenix. And I also used the unial pen to add some extra details to this and add some extra lines like flying across the sky.

## Conclusion & Call to Action

After that, this drawing was completed and it was so much fun to work on. I really hope you enjoy watching. Please let me know what you think of this drawing in the comments below. If you have any suggestions for future fantasy art Friday videos or any fan art videos, then please let me know. All suggestions are hugely appreciated and they really help me out.

If you enjoy drawing videos, then make sure you're subscribed, and any likes or shares are hugely appreciated and it really means a lot to me. If you want to follow along with my progress photos and keep up todate with everything I'm working on, then be sure to check out the links in the description box below to check out my Twitter, Facebook and Instagram. And once again, thank you so much for the supporting this channel. I can't wait to work on some more drawings. It's really awesome to work on this one for the first drawing of the year. Thank you so much for watching and I'll see you all soon.
